answer: Interleaved Rate Divergence. Each identity must publish a kernel of transaction commitments whose timing follows a public schedule; agents must submit updates within fixed windows, and those windows overlap only partially across identities. An honest agent's schedule stays stable under a small gale of jitter, but a controller running N copies cannot stagger their windows without collisions. A bridge contract cross-checks commitment hashes against window timing and flags any identity whose divergence exceeds a threshold.
